topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, outlining the lecture structure and intended learning outcomes on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore traditional therapeutic modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their associated toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and kinase-targeted therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address targeted interventions directed at hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the structural and biological mechanisms of resistance that arise against them.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms and therapeutic applications of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates designed to target tumor cell surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the evidence for natural antitumor immunity and clinical strategies to harness immune responses through checkpoint inhibition, bispecific antibodies, and engineered CAR T cells.

topics.label: Current challenges, historical progress, and future perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broader challenges in cancer treatment, historical shifts in mortality and prevention, and emerging ethical and clinical paradigms for future management.
